content:
Anthropic has released its latest AI model, Claude Opus 5.5. The new version comes roughly two months after the previous Opus model upgrade, in line with Anthropic's usual release cadence.

Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5

Anthropic's Claude family currently offers multiple AI models.

The three flagship models are Haiku (smallest and cheapest), Sonnet (mid-tier in size and pricing), and Opus (the largest and most expensive of the three).

In addition, there is Fable/Mythos, which offers even more powerful capabilities at a higher price, representing Anthropic's top-tier positioning.

This release upgrades the Opus model in the Claude family from version 5.0 to version 5.5.

Anthropic stated: "Opus 5.5 is the first model we've launched since calling for a slowdown in frontier development. As with previous models, it was tested by external evaluators before release, including METR and Frontier Design. In our most comprehensive alignment evaluations, it achieved the highest score to date."

Below is Anthropic's introduction of Opus 5.5's performance:

Regarding coding, Anthropic had this to say:

Opus 5.5 is particularly adept at handling large and wide-ranging tasks, such as migrating and auditing entire codebases. One early tester used it to review and patch a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours, whereas Opus 5 required over 20 hours and used 2.5 times more resources. In an internal test, we had Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 translate HAProxy (a software widely used to balance network traffic loads across servers) from C to Rust. Both rewrites passed nearly all of HAProxy's own regression tests, but Opus 5.5 completed the task in just 9.5 hours, faster than Fable 5.1's 12 hours, and at 51% lower cost. Opus 5.5 delivers frontier-level agentic coding performance at a fraction of the cost of its peers. On FrontierCode's default workload settings, it outperformed GPT-6 Astra at roughly 20% of the cost per task. On Terminal Bench 4.0, it tied with Astra at only about 40% of the cost; on CursorBench, it led GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at approximately one-third the cost.

In addition, pricing for Opus 5.5 has been adjusted compared to Opus 5:

Opus 5.5 requires less compute to run than Opus 5, and pricing reflects this accordingly. Our testing shows that on default settings, it costs 40% less than Opus 5 for typical workloads. Input and output tokens are priced at $4 and $20 per million respectively, 20% lower than Opus 5. Cache reads (which account for the majority of cost in agentic and coding workloads) are priced at $0.20 per million tokens, 60% lower than Opus 5. Opus 5.5 also outputs over 30% faster than Opus 5. Beyond the price reductions, we have also increased the five-hour usage limits for Pro, Max, and Team plans. We are also offering usage credit resets for subscribers, which you can now save and use whenever you need them.

The new Claude Opus 5.5 model is now officially available. Looking ahead, Anthropic said Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be "released in the coming weeks, bringing similar improvements in performance, efficiency, and safety."
